# ethereum-optimism/ecosystem Weekly Report (May 31 - June 6, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week’s development focused on hardening the infrastructure for the Superchain’s interoperability layer and streamlining the developer environment. Significant progress was made toward launching a long-running devnet, while the team addressed critical recovery challenges related to interop transaction pools and invalid message handling. Technical efforts also prioritized build reliability through Docker optimizations and strategic synchronization of the `op-revm` stack with upstream releases to support upcoming hardforks.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Infrastructure & Build Reliability
Efforts were directed at improving the stability of the development environment and containerization process.
*   **Docker Build Optimization:** A critical fix was implemented to ensure Docker builds ignore lifecycle scripts during dependency installation. This change enhances build reliability and prevents unnecessary script execution during the container assembly process ([#1007](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/pull/1007)).

### Protocol & Execution Layer Synchronization
The team is focusing on maintaining parity with the broader Ethereum execution layer ecosystem.
*   **`op-revm` Alignment:** Ongoing work is centered on synchronizing `op-revm` with the latest `revm` releases (specifically v111). This alignment is crucial for Amsterdam hardfork support and shared type definitions. The team is also updating internal guides to ensure more proactive dependency updates in coordination with `reth` ([#21069](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/21069)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### New & Active Issues
The week's triage activity highlighted specific technical hurdles in the interoperability (interop) framework and devnet deployment.

*   **Interop Recovery Challenges:** Two significant issues were identified regarding system resilience during interop failures. First, a bug in `op-reth` prevents the transaction pool from resuming interop transactions after a failsafe is disabled without a full restart of `op-reth` and `op-rbuilder` ([#21149](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/21149)). Second, the team proposed creating a formal runbook to handle large reorgs triggered by invalid interop messages, as current systems do not yet handle these events smoothly ([#21161](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/21161)).
*   **Devnet Deployment:** Progress continues on spinning up a long-running devnet. The current blocker is the availability of `glamsterdam-devnet-4` images, which are required before the full infrastructure can be deployed ([#20691](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/20691)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
Collaboration this week was characterized by deep technical planning around execution layer dependencies. Discussions regarding `op-revm` indicate a high level of coordination between protocol developers to ensure the OP Stack remains compatible with the latest Ethereum standards. The focus on creating runbooks for interop failures suggests a proactive, community-oriented approach to documenting operational procedures for future Superchain participants.
